headline: North Korea crossed the 38th parallel, McCarthy claimed 205 Communists, and Peanuts began in seven newspapers
texture: North Korean troops and T-34 tanks crossed the 38th parallel on June 25 and took Seoul three days later. South Korean engineers blew the Hangang Bridge while it was crowded with refugees, North Korean troops killed around 800 staff and patients at Seoul National University Hospital, and South Korean forces and police began the Bodo League executions, at least 100,000 people suspected of sympathy with the north. The 24th Infantry Division lost Taejon in July, and the delay let the Pusan Perimeter be established.

Joseph McCarthy told a Republican women's club at the McClure Hotel in Wheeling on February 9 that the State Department was full of 205 Communists. Klaus Fuchs had walked into the War Office in London on January 24 and confessed to seven years of passing nuclear weapons research to the Soviet Union. Red Channels, a report on communist influence in radio and television, was published in June. Griselio Torresola and Oscar Collazo tried to kill Truman at the Blair-Lee House on November 1, where he was living while the White House was repaired.

Truth or Consequences moved from radio to CBS television on September 7, You Bet Your Life followed to NBC on October 4, and Your Hit Parade had crossed in July. Desi Arnaz and Lucille Ball founded Desilu Productions in May. The FCC approved the CBS color system in October, due to take effect on November 20, and RCA disputed the license and blocked it. Radio was still ordering new shows, and NBC put Tallulah Bankhead in front of The Big Show on November 5.

Sam Phillips opened Sun Records at 706 Union Avenue in Memphis on January 3. Eleven thieves took more than two million dollars from an armored car in Boston on January 17. Zenith marketed the first television remote control, called Lazy Bones. Gwendolyn Brooks won the Pulitzer for poetry on May 1, the first African American to win one. Polio went through Wythe County, Virginia, over the summer, 189 cases and 17 deaths. Johann Sebastian Bach was reburied in St. Thomas Church in Leipzig.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Alben W. Barkley was Vice President, Fred M. Vinson was Chief Justice, and the 81st Congress sat.

pol.h_bomb.label: Truman orders the hydrogen bomb
pol.h_bomb.value: Ordered its development in response to the Soviet Union's first atomic test
pol.h_bomb.detail: NSC 68, issued on April 14 and approved on September 30, argued for building it, for military aid to allies and for rolling back communist expansion.

pol.red_scare.label: McCarthy at Wheeling
pol.red_scare.value: Told the Republican Women's Club at the McClure Hotel that the State Department was filled with 205 Communists
pol.red_scare.detail: Alger Hiss was convicted of perjury on January 21. Klaus Fuchs confessed to spying on January 24 and was convicted in London on March 1. A Senate subcommittee report made public on December 15 recommended against federal employment of homosexuals.

pol.blair_house.label: Attempt on Truman's life
pol.blair_house.value: Griselio Torresola and Oscar Collazo tried to kill Truman at the Blair-Lee House, where he was staying during White House repairs
pol.blair_house.detail: The Jayuya Uprising against US rule in Puerto Rico had begun on October 30.

pol.sweatt.label: Sweatt v. Painter
pol.sweatt.value: The Supreme Court decided a challenge to the separate but equal doctrine in education

world.korea_begins.label: The Korean War begins
world.korea_begins.value: North Korean troops and T-34 tanks crossed the 38th parallel, and Seoul fell on June 28
world.korea_begins.detail: Truman ordered American forces to the defence of South Korea on June 27. The South Korean army blew up the Hangang Bridge while it was crowded with refugees, and the Bodo League executions of at least 100,000 suspected sympathizers began.

world.inchon.label: Battle of Inchon
world.inchon.value: Allied troops under Douglas MacArthur landed at Inchon to begin a UN counteroffensive

world.china_enters.label: China enters the war
world.china_enters.value: Thousands of Chinese soldiers crossed the Yalu River
world.china_enters.detail: A counterattack at the Ch'ongch'on River and the Chosin Reservoir followed on November 26, and MacArthur threatened to use nuclear weapons on November 30. On November 8 an American F-80 shot down two MiG-15s near the Yalu in the first jet-to-jet dogfight.

world.uk_election.label: United Kingdom general election
world.uk_election.value: Labour under Clement Attlee stayed in office while the Conservatives under Winston Churchill gained seats

world.india_republic.label: India becomes a republic
world.india_republic.value: Promulgated its constitution, and Rajendra Prasad was sworn in as its first president
world.india_republic.detail: The Kingdom of Mysore was merged into the new republic.

world.schuman.label: Schuman Declaration
world.schuman.value: Robert Schuman proposed a pan-European organisation, which he called indispensable to permanently peaceful relations between the nations of the continent

world.tibet.label: China annexes Tibet
world.tibet.value: The People's Liberation Army invaded across the Jinsha River, took the border town of Chamdo by October 19, and the Tibetan army surrendered
world.tibet.detail: Tenzin Gyatso, aged 15, was enthroned as the 14th Dalai Lama and temporal ruler of Tibet on November 17.

world.group_areas.label: Group Areas Act
world.group_areas.value: South Africa passed the act formally segregating the races
world.group_areas.detail: The Suppression of Communism Act, passed on June 26, came into force on July 17.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, US domestic rentals
value: Samson and Delilah, $9,000,000, Paramount
King Solomon's Mines, $5,047,000, MGM
Annie Get Your Gun, $4,708,000, MGM
Cheaper by the Dozen, $4,425,000, 20th Century Fox
Cinderella, $4,275,000, RKO and Walt Disney
film.gross.detail: Rentals, the distributor share rather than the ticket window total, so roughly half what a gross figure would say. Cinderella was the studio's most successful film since Dumbo and cleared four million dollars of Disney debt.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following spring at the 23rd Academy Awards. It arrived with a record fourteen nominations, past a previous record of thirteen, and won six.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Jose Ferrer, Cyrano de Bergerac
Best Actress, Judy Holliday, Born Yesterday
Best Supporting Actor, George Sanders, All About Eve
Best Supporting Actress, Josephine Hull, Harvey
film.acting_awards.detail: All About Eve took four of the female acting nominations, two for Best Actress and two for Best Supporting Actress, and none of them won. Sunset Boulevard had a nomination in every acting category and won none either.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, city by city rather than everywhere at once. Samson and Delilah played New York for three weeks before it opened in Los Angeles on January 13.

film.world_cinema.label: Outside Hollywood
value: Rashomon, directed by Akira Kurosawa, Japan
Los Olvidados, directed by Luis Bunuel, Mexico
Orphee, directed by Jean Cocteau, France

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, the first Nielsen season
value: Texaco Star Theater, NBC, 61.6 rating
Fireside Theatre, NBC, 52.6
Philco TV Playhouse, NBC, 45.3
Your Show of Shows, NBC, 42.6
The Colgate Comedy Hour, NBC, 42.0
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that began in the autumn and ran into the following spring. The top six programs were all on NBC.

tv.premieres.label: Programs that debuted
value: What's My Line, CBS, February 2
Your Show of Shows, NBC, February 25
Truth or Consequences, CBS, September 7, from radio
The Colgate Comedy Hour, NBC, September 10
You Bet Your Life, NBC, October 4, from radio

tv.color.label: Color television approved
tv.color.value: The FCC approved the CBS color system, with approval due to take effect on November 20
tv.color.detail: RCA disputed the licence and blocked it from taking effect. The US year page dates the licence to October 11 rather than October 10.

tv.desilu.label: Desilu Productions founded
tv.desilu.value: Desi Arnaz and Lucille Ball set up their own television production company

radio.radio_free_europe.label: Radio Free Europe begins
radio.radio_free_europe.value: Broadcast 30 minutes of American programming to Czechoslovakia from a 7,500 watt short wave transmitter at Lampertheim in West Germany
radio.radio_free_europe.detail: Romania became the second communist country sent broadcasts from the station, on July 14.

radio.red_channels.label: Red Channels
radio.red_channels.value: Red Channels: The Report of Communist Influence in Radio and Television was published

music.chart_toppers.label: Records that reached number one
value: Goodnight, Irene, Gordon Jenkins and The Weavers, 13 weeks
The Third Man Theme, Anton Karas, 11 weeks
The Tennessee Waltz, Patti Page, 9 weeks from December 30
Mona Lisa, Nat King Cole, 5 weeks
Music! Music! Music!, Teresa Brewer, 4 weeks
music.chart_toppers.detail: From Billboard's charts, ordered by weeks at the top. Twelve records reached number one during the year, beginning with Gene Autry's Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer in the first week of January. Patti Page became the first artist to hold a number one on the pop, rhythm and blues and country charts concurrently.

music.sun_records.label: Sun Records launched
music.sun_records.value: Sam Phillips started the label at 706 Union Avenue in Memphis

music.bach.label: Bach reburied
music.bach.value: Johann Sebastian Bach was reburied in St. Thomas Church, Leipzig

tech.diners_club.label: First charge card payment
tech.diners_club.value: A payment was made with a Diners Club card in New York, the first use of a charge card

tech.remote_control.label: Television remote control
tech.remote_control.value: Zenith Radio marketed the Lazy Bones, the first television remote control

tech.californium.label: Element 98
tech.californium.value: Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley announced its creation and named it californium

tech.turing_test.label: Turing test proposed
tech.turing_test.value: Alan Turing published Computing Machinery and Intelligence in the journal Mind, replacing the question of whether a machine can think with a test of whether it can be told apart from a person
tech.turing_test.detail: The year page dates it to October and says nothing further, so the description comes from the paper's own page.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Leaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: A war in Asia five years after the last one finished, senators hunting communists in the State Department and in broadcasting studios, and a television set arriving on the street.

culture.peanuts.label: Peanuts begins
culture.peanuts.value: Charles M. Schulz's comic strip was first published in seven US newspapers

culture.brooks.label: Pulitzer Prize for Poetry
culture.brooks.value: Gwendolyn Brooks won it for Annie Allen, the first African American to win a Pulitzer

sports.world_cup.label: World Cup
sports.world_cup.value: Uruguay beat Brazil 2 to 1 in the deciding match at the Maracana, remembered as the Maracanazo
sports.world_cup.detail: The stadium had opened on June 16, eight days before the tournament began. The United States beat England 1 to 0 in the group stage on June 29.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: New York Yankees swept the Philadelphia Phillies four games to none, their 13th title

sports.nfl_championship.label: NFL Championship
sports.nfl_championship.value: Cleveland Browns beat the Los Angeles Rams 30 to 28 at Cleveland Stadium

sports.f1.label: Formula One World Championship
sports.f1.value: The first championship race was run at Silverstone, and Giuseppe Farina took the title
sports.f1.detail: Farina became the first champion on September 3.

sports.stanley_cup.label: Stanley Cup
sports.stanley_cup.value: Detroit Red Wings beat the New York Rangers four games to three

deaths.shaw.label: George Bernard Shaw
deaths.shaw.detail: Irish writer and Nobel laureate in literature.

deaths.jolson.label: Al Jolson
deaths.jolson.detail: American singer and actor, who starred in The Jazz Singer.

deaths.smuts.label: Jan Smuts
deaths.smuts.detail: Second Prime Minister of South Africa.

notes: Research pass July 2026. The box office table header states domestic rentals, so figures_basis is rentals. Deaths carry a birth year rather than an age because the source gives only the year. The Nielsen ranking is a season that starts in the autumn of 1950 and runs into the spring of 1951, so the fact says the first Nielsen season instead of naming both years. Truman's hydrogen bomb order responded to the Soviet atomic test of 1949, which the fact cannot date because no other year token may appear in a fact string. Two cached sources disagree on colour television: the American television page dates the FCC approval of the CBS system to October 10 with effect from November 20 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_in_American_television), and the US year page dates the first colour licence to October 11 and records RCA blocking it (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_in_the_United_States). Both are cited on the fact. Dropped for lack of a settled source: the pilot of The Archers, which the year page dates May 29 and the radio page June 7; the claim that one million American households owned a television set, which the television page carries with a citation needed tag. The Diners Club line on the year page is tagged as needing a better source and is kept anyway, flagged here, because it is the only cached statement of the first charge card payment. The year page gives the Turing test only as "October - Turing test published", so tech.turing_test cites https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computing_Machinery_and_Intelligence for the paper's title, journal and argument, and keeps the year page's month. Samson and Delilah tops the rentals table for this year although its world premiere came in the previous December, three weeks before its Los Angeles opening on January 13, which is the basis the film page uses. Nothing in the prose or the facts comes from general knowledge; the polio outbreak in Wythe County, the Brinks robbery figure and the Bach reburial are all on the cached pages.
